title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The page computes the graded duals of the PD de Rham complex A_n of the algebraic n-simplex. It does this in a homogenized form, with an auxiliary variable T replacing the equation ΣX_i = 1 by ΣX_i = T, so that everything is graded. Only the two extreme exterior degrees are treated.

(1) Exterior degree 0. A_n^0 ≃ k{{T}}{{X_0..X_n}}/(ΣX_i − T)_pd. This is the quotient of the free PD algebra by the PD ideal generated by ΣX_i − T. Eliminating T gives A_n^0 ≃ k{{X_0..X_n}}, the divided-power polynomial algebra. Equivalently it is the image of the PD-algebra epimorphism k{{T,X_0..X_n}} → k{{X_0..X_n}} with X_i ↦ X_i and T ↦ ΣX_i.

(2) Duality in degree 0. The pairing ⟨X^{(i)}, Z^j⟩ = δ_{i,j} identifies the graded dual of a PD polynomial algebra with an ordinary polynomial algebra. The dual of the epimorphism above is the monomorphism k[Z_0..Z_n] → k[U,Y_0..Y_n] with Z_i ↦ U + Y_i. Here U is dual to T and Y_i is dual to X_i, with ⟨T^{(λ)}X^{(i)}, U^μ Y^j⟩ = δ_{λμ} δ_{ij}.
- The image is the joint kernel of all divided powers D^{(m)} of D = Σ ∂/∂Y_i − ∂/∂U.
- Divided powers are needed because k may have positive characteristic.
- So (A^n)_0 ≃ k[Z_0..Z_n].

(3) Top part (complementary degree 0). A_n^{*=*} ≃ Λ_k[dX_0..dX_n]/(ΣdX_i), a quotient of Λ_k[dX_0..dX_n].
- Its dual is Λ_k([Y_0..Y_n]'), where [Y_0..Y_n]' is the hyperplane of vectors with coordinate sum 0.
- This sits inside Λ_k[Y_0..Y_n] as the kernel of the interior product i_X, where X is the linear form 'sum of coordinates'.
- NB: from 0 → [Y]' → [Y] → k → 0 there is a canonical isomorphism det([Y]') ≃ det([Y]) ⊗ k^∨ ≃ k.

(4) Conclusion. There is a canonical isomorphism (A^n)_n ≃ (A^n)_0 ≃ k[Z_0..Z_n], twisted by the canonical generator of the top exterior power. This is then used to define a map K_n : k[U] → k[Z_0..Z_n]. That map is presumably the dual of the integration/trace (or coaugmentation) structure on the simplex. It sets up a 'polynomial chain' model dual to the cosimplicial PD de Rham forms.

Purpose: show that the PD de Rham forms on the standard simplices (the PD analogue of Sullivan/Cartan polynomial forms, valid over any base ring) have computable, explicitly dual chain-level models.

(The neighbouring pages in the scan are unrelated SGA 7 IX material on reused paper.)
errors: NB line: the exact sequence 0 → [Y_0..Y_n]' → [Y_0..Y_n] → k → 0 gives Λ^n([Y]') ≃ Λ^{n+1}([Y]) ≃ k. The middle term should be Λ^{n+1}, not Λ^n (possibly a misreading of the handwriting).
Minor: the exact sequence is written without the initial 0.
The bracket notation ([..]^! vs [..]') is used inconsistently.

Otherwise the computations check. The duality of D(T↦ΣX_i) matches the binomial expansion of Π(U+Y_α)^{j_α}. In coordinates (U, Z_i = U+Y_i) one has D = −∂/∂U, so the joint kernel of the D^{(m)} is k[Z]. The kernel of i_X equals Λ(ker X) because X ≠ 0.

ideas.what: PD de Rham complex of the algebraic n-simplex, homogenized via T, as a cosimplicial model for cochains over any ring
ideas.modern_name: simplicial divided-power de Rham forms (PD analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (Théories cohomologiques, Invent. Math. 1976); Sullivan for the rational case

ideas.what: Graded duality between divided-power polynomial algebras and polynomial algebras; dual of PD quotient is the joint kernel of divided powers of a derivation
ideas.modern_name: Γ(V)^∨ ≅ Sym(V^∨); Hasse–Schmidt / divided-power differential operators
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §16 for divided-power differential operators

ideas.what: Dual of top exterior part as Λ of the sum-zero hyperplane = ker of interior product; canonical orientation from the determinant of the exact sequence
ideas.modern_name: Koszul/determinant identification, orientation of the simplex

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up explicit graded duals (polynomial chain models) of the simplicial PD de Rham forms, ending with a map K_n: k[U] → k[Z_0..Z_n]. This points toward a polynomial 'chains' coalgebra model dual to PD forms over arbitrary rings. The thread is not developed on this page.
missed.quote: Donc (A^n)_n ≃ (A^n)_0 ≃ k[Z_0,…,Z_n] … donc K_n : k[U] → k[Z_0,…,Z_n]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and PD models of cochains (Cartan, Mandell, PD/E∞ approaches, Bhatt–Lurie-style derived de Rham) still look for explicit chain-level duals. This is likely of modest novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine dualities computed carefully. Interest lies in documenting the content of Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 PD de Rham talk, which parallels Cartan's contemporaneous work.
transcription_corrections: NB: should read Λ^n([Y_0..Y_n]') ≃ Λ^{n+1}([Y_0..Y_n]) ≃ k, with exact sequence 0 → [Y]' → [Y] → k → 0.
'ss-ev.' = sous-espace vectoriel; [Y_0..Y_n]^! is the same object as [Y_0..Y_n]'.
The monomorphism target is k[U][Y_0..Y_n] ≅ k[U,Y_0..Y_n].
